name: en-analytics-late-breach
modelledOn: A product analytics vendor's agreement, complete on paper, whose breach notice is measured in business days.
text:
Metrix Analytics Data Processing Agreement

This Data Processing Agreement is entered into between Metrix Analytics GmbH, Torstraße 100, 10119 Berlin ("Metrix", acting as processor) and the customer identified in the Metrix account ("Customer", acting as controller), and governs the processing of personal data by Metrix on behalf of Customer in connection with the Metrix analytics service.

1. Duration and subject-matter. The processing covers the collection and analysis of usage events from Customer's websites and applications and continues for as long as Customer maintains a Metrix account, after which section 12 applies.

2. Nature and purpose. Metrix receives events generated by Customer's end users, stores them, aggregates them into reports and dashboards and makes those available to Customer, for the purpose of letting Customer understand how its products are used.

3. Data and data subjects. The personal data consists of pseudonymous user identifiers, device and browser characteristics, IP addresses truncated on receipt, page and screen views, in-app events and any custom properties Customer chooses to send; the data subjects are the end users of Customer's websites and applications.

4. Customer. Customer is responsible for the lawfulness of the collection, for informing its end users and obtaining any consent required, for the instructions it gives through the Metrix configuration, and may exercise the rights of information, audit and objection set out in this Agreement.

5. Instructions. Metrix will process personal data only on documented instructions from Customer, including with regard to transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law to which Metrix is subject, in which case Metrix will inform Customer of that legal requirement before processing unless that law prohibits such information.

6. Personnel. Metrix ensures that persons authorised to process the personal data have committed themselves to confidentiality under their employment or service contracts.

7. Security. Metrix implements the technical and organisational measures described in Annex 2, which include encryption in transit and at rest, access on a need-to-know basis, separation of customer data by tenant, continuous monitoring and an annual independent penetration test.

8. Sub-processors. Customer grants Metrix general authorisation to engage the sub-processors listed in Annex 3, each of which is bound by a written agreement imposing data protection obligations equivalent to those in this Agreement. Metrix will notify Customer by email at least 30 days before it adds or replaces a sub-processor, and Customer may object to the change within 30 days of the notice; if Metrix cannot accommodate the objection Customer may terminate the affected service.

9. Data subject requests. Metrix will assist Customer, by appropriate technical and organisational measures, in fulfilling Customer's obligation to respond to requests by data subjects to exercise their rights, and will forward to Customer any request it receives directly.

10. Compliance assistance. Metrix will assist Customer in ensuring compliance with the obligations pursuant to Articles 32 to 36 of the GDPR, taking into account the nature of the processing and the information available to Metrix.

11. Personal data breach. Metrix will notify Customer of a personal data breach affecting Customer's personal data within 5 business days of becoming aware of it and will provide reasonable assistance with Customer's notification obligations.

12. Return and deletion. Upon termination of the service Metrix will, at Customer's election, return the personal data in a commonly used format or delete it, and will delete existing copies within 90 days unless Union or Member State law requires storage.

13. Audit. Metrix will make available to Customer all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with this Agreement and will allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by Customer or an auditor mandated by Customer, provided the auditor is bound by confidentiality and the audit is announced 30 days in advance.

14. International transfers. Where a sub-processor in Annex 3 is located outside the European Economic Area, Metrix relies on the standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission, which are incorporated into this Agreement as Annex 4 and executed between Metrix and that sub-processor.

Annex 1: Details of processing. Annex 2: Security measures. Annex 3: Sub-processors. Annex 4: Standard contractual clauses.

reasoning: Every element is present and quoted. The breach notice, however, allows five business days, at least 120 hours, so the controller's own 72 hours from becoming aware would be gone before it hears; the check fails and the agreement is inadequate on that alone. Sub-processor changes carry 30 days' notice and an objection; transfers rest on the standard contractual clauses in Annex 4.
